svg.text: BACK · SPINE · WINGS · CHEST-LOCK, UNWRAPPED OVER THE SHOULDERS
Master line-work, 49 kill-tally blades. Chest panel is drawn flipped upward across the shoulder fold.
Arm-shaft: wing-root lock to joint lock to joint lock, then
Four rib-staves a wing, each ending in an inward talon kink.
Kill-tally blades ride the trailing side only: 4 · 6 · 7 · 7 =
Hairline counter-ticks are ornament, not tallies. One
Blade: a solid sliver 38° off the stave, point trailing to the talon.
Counter-tick: a hairline on the leading side, never counted.
The clavicle staves cross above the heart, one over, one
under, and run on to the far corners.
Each deltoid stave turns at its knee lock, weaves through, and
stops short: the lowest point stays open.
Quartered eclipse at the heart; one hollow blade beneath,
Three pinions a side hang from the deltoid stave: notched,
Nothing rises above the collar line. Throat and neck stay
